full_name: Meta frontier AI risk framework (Advanced AI Scaling Framework)
mission: Included only for its published catastrophic-risk policy, not Meta's products. Meta's Frontier AI Framework (Feb 2025) — revised as the Advanced AI Scaling Framework v2 (Apr 2026) — defines outcome-based 'moderate', 'high' and 'critical' risk thresholds for cybersecurity, chemical & biological weapons and (from v2) loss of control. Meta does not run a large public-facing alignment research team comparable to the other labs; its earlier Responsible AI team was broken up in 2023 (widely reported).

key_work.title: Frontier AI Framework
key_work.plain_summary: Meta's first frontier safety policy: if a model would 'uniquely enable' a catastrophic cyber or chem/bio threat scenario and cannot be mitigated, Meta says it will stop development.

key_work.title: Advanced AI Scaling Framework v2.0
key_work.plain_summary: April 2026 revision adding Loss of Control as a third catastrophic-risk domain and changing the threshold standard to whether a model would 'substantially contribute to' a catastrophic outcome.

warnings.text: Frontier AI could enable catastrophic outcomes in cybersecurity (e.g. automated end-to-end compromise of a well-protected corporate network) and chemical & biological weapons.
From v2 (2026), loss of control — failures of critical oversight of AI systems — is treated as a catastrophic-risk domain.

recommendations.text: If a model reaches the critical risk threshold and cannot be mitigated, stop development; high-risk models must not be released until mitigated.
Use threat modelling and red-teaming with external experts once models reach relevant capability levels.
